name: Avianca Cargo red livery (2013)
description: Avianca's 2013 red scheme on the freighters: a white fuselage with red 'Avianca Cargo' over the forward fuselage ('Avianca' bold, 'Cargo' light) and Avianca's red bird ahead of it; a red swoosh rising from the belly into the fin, so the whole tail is red; an orange dorsal fillet; a red fin faceted in darker red with a white panel at the tip; red engines with a white bird and white inlets; red winglets.

A333.note: The A330-300P2Fs (Avianca Cargo México's N337QT, LAX 2026-08-04) were painted red after the 2023 rebrand, in a plainer form: no swoosh and no orange (the fuselage all white, the fillet red), lowercase 'avianca' (bold) and 'cargo' (light) with an x-height of about 1.05 m, red engines to the lip, the fin's dark facet down to the root. Left side measured; the right side's titles are placed as the A332's run (cargo ahead of avianca). Its small 'Mexico' under 'avianca' is left out.

notes: The red Avianca scheme Avianca Cargo's A330-200Fs were delivered in from 2013 (N334QT at Toulouse, 2013-09), drawn as N336QT and N332QT wore it at Miami in 2023-01. Measured on N336QT's right side, flipped and fitted to shapes/A332.json: the swoosh's front edge leaves the belly about 37 m back and meets the crown at the fin's root (49 m); the tail cone's end is left white. 'Avianca' runs x 0.273-0.402 and 'Cargo' 0.164-0.264 with 1.4 m capitals, the bird centred at x 0.138. The fleet's red paint varies: N336QT has been retitled in the 2023 lowercase 'avianca cargo' (2024-08) with the swoosh kept, and repaints since lack the swoosh and orange (N330QT, ex-Tampa Cargo, with capital titles in 2024-12; N337QT with lowercase titles in 2026-08). The A333 paint here is that plainer form, as on N337QT. The country's flag under the cockpit and at the fin's tip and the IATA CEIV Fresh badges some aircraft carry are left out. Avianca Cargo's green scheme (TPA/standard) has replaced this on some aircraft since 2025.
